Info:

jellify (verb) - to make gelatinous see also.

Jellify is a free and open source music player for the Jellyfin Media Server. Built with React Native, it is available for both iOS and Android.

Showcasing the artwork of your library, it has a user interface congruent to what the big guys do. Jellify also provides algorithmic curation of your music, driven by Jellyfin's Instant Mix and Suggestions APIs.

This app was designed with me and my dad in mind. I wanted us to have a sleek, one stop shop for live recordings of bands we like (read: the Grateful Dead). The UI was designed so that we'd find it instantly familiar and useful. CarPlay / Android Auto support was also a must for us, as we both use CarPlay religiously.

versions.localizedDescription:
Welcome to Jellify 1.4.0.

I am so excited to share all the wonderful improvements we have packed into this latest version! We have introduced some amazing new features like CarPlay support and several polish updates to your favorite interface elements. This update is all about making your music experience smoother, faster, and more enjoyable for everyone.

• We have officially added CarPlay support, which includes a dedicated library tab for your road trips. We also introduced a new Your Playlists section and renamed the Add to Queue button to Play Later to make the app even more intuitive.

• You will notice much faster loading times when browsing your music library thanks to some significant performance optimizations. We also upgraded our internal caching system to ensure your favorite playlists are always ready to play.

Issues addressed:

• [FEATURE] Add Ability to Switch App Icons (#370).
• [BUG] Failed to "Play Next" with an Empty Queue (#551).
• [BUG] Server Version not updating (#745).

• [BUG] Skipping next on the last track ignores "Repeat All" and stops playback (#1467).
• [BUG] lyrics on white background (#1491).
• [FEATURE] Centralized caches for user and public playlists (#1572).
• [BUG] Shuffle toggle is slow — icon lags because tracks are removed one-by-one over the bridge (#1592).
